# Backends: which program each route runs

<!-- Generated by tools/backends_doc.py from dev/backends.json and dev/backend_usage.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

`pat` is a thin wrapper: every development route runs one upstream program as a child process,
records its exact command line and log in the job receipt, and checks the result instead of
trusting the exit status. This page lists those programs, what the toolkit runs them with, and
on which platforms `pat dev setup` has a pinned download. Nothing here is redistributed; each
program keeps its own license (see `NOTICE`). Regenerate with `python tools/backends_doc.py --write`.

`<...>` is a value the toolkit fills in per job; `[...]` is optional. The `<out>` directory is the
job's new `--output`; inputs are staged inside it before the program runs.

## Programs the toolkit runs

### OpenAssetTools 0.33.0

- Upstream: <https://github.com/Laupetin/OpenAssetTools>
- License: GPL-3.0
- Pinned downloads: windows: `oat-windows.zip`; linux: `oat-linux.tar.gz`
- Binaries: `Linker.exe` / `Linker` as `PAT_BACKEND_LINKER`, `Unlinker.exe` / `Unlinker` as `PAT_BACKEND_UNLINKER`, `ImageConverter.exe` / `ImageConverter` as `PAT_BACKEND_IMAGE`

| Routes | Command line | What the toolkit checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ff link`, `project build`, `module build` | `Linker --no-color --base-folder <project> --output-folder <out>/packages [--add-asset-search-path <dir>]... [-l <zone.ff>]... <zone>` | a .ff was produced; every package is read back with Unlinker |
| `ff inspect`, `ff link`, `project build`, `module build`, `module declare` | `Unlinker --no-color --skip-obj --list [-l <zone.ff>]... <fastfile>` | readback log has no load failure; inventory kept as a job log |
| `ff extract`, `project build`, `module build`, `module declare` | `Unlinker --no-color --output-folder <out>/assets [--model-format <fmt>] [--image-format <fmt>] [--include-assets <types>] [-l <zone.ff>]... <fastfile>` | files were written; project build byte-compares every rawfile against its source |
| `image convert` | `ImageConverter --no-color --<t6\|t5> <image.dds\|image.iwi>` | a non-empty converted image exists beside the staged input |

### gsc-tool 1.4.10

- Upstream: <https://github.com/xensik/gsc-tool>
- License: GPL-3.0
- Pinned downloads: windows: `windows-x64-release.zip`; linux: `linux-amd64-release.tar.gz`
- Binaries: `gsc-tool.exe` / `gsc-tool` as `PAT_BACKEND_GSC`

| Routes | Command line | What the toolkit checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gsc compile`, `gsc decompile`, `project build`, `module build` | `gsc-tool -m <comp\|decomp> -g t6 -s pc -i <server\|client> [-w <includes>] <script>` | exit status, error lines in the log, non-empty output files |

### CoDLuaDecompiler 2.4.2

- Upstream: <https://github.com/JariKCoding/CoDLuaDecompiler>
- License: MIT
- Pinned downloads: windows: `CoDLuaDecompiler.zip`
- Binaries: `CoDLuaDecompiler.exe` / `CoDLuaDecompiler` as `PAT_BACKEND_LUA`
- Note: Windows only (.NET build). On Linux set PAT_BACKEND_LUA to a working CoDLuaDecompiler if you have one; no Linux download is pinned.

| Routes | Command line | What the toolkit checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lua decompile` | `CoDLuaDecompiler <out>/input.lua` | a non-empty decompiled .lua exists beside the staged input |

### FFmpeg 9.0 (BtbN gpl builds)

- Upstream: <https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds>
- License: GPL-2.0-or-later (build); see upstream
- Pinned downloads: windows: `ffmpeg-n9.0.1-27-g9b0578816c-win64-gpl-shared-9.0.zip`; linux: `ffmpeg-n9.0.1-27-g9b0578816c-linux64-gpl-9.0.tar.xz`
- Binaries: `bin/ffmpeg.exe` / `bin/ffmpeg` as `PAT_BACKEND_FFMPEG`, `bin/ffprobe.exe` / `bin/ffprobe` as `PAT_BACKEND_FFPROBE`

| Routes | Command line | What the toolkit checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audio inspect`, `audio convert` | `ffprobe -v error -show_format -show_streams -of json <file>` | JSON with at least one audio stream; after convert, sample rate and channels match the request |
| `audio convert` | `ffmpeg -nostdin -v error -n -i <src> -map 0:a:0 -vn -ar <rate> -ac <1\|2> -c:a <pcm_s16le\|flac\|libvorbis\|libmp3lame> <out>/audio.<format>` | non-empty output, then ffprobe verifies the stream parameters |

### Blender 5.2.1

- Upstream: <https://www.blender.org>
- License: GPL-3.0
- Pinned downloads: windows: `blender-5.2.1-windows-x64.zip`; linux: `blender-5.2.1-linux-x64.tar.xz`
- Binaries: `blender.exe` / `blender` as `PAT_BACKEND_BLENDER`

| Routes | Command line | What the toolkit checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model inspect`, `model convert`, `model transform`, `model rename-bones`, `model retime`, `model preview` | `blender --background --factory-startup --disable-autoexec --threads 2 --python-exit-code 1 --python <toolkit>/dev/blender_worker.py -- <out>/request.json` | the worker writes model-result.json; outputs must exist and be non-empty. The Cast add-on is loaded by path from the cast backend directory |

## Add-ons loaded by another program

### Cast Blender add-on 2.00

- Upstream: <https://github.com/dtzxporter/cast>
- License: MIT
- Pinned download: any platform (pure Python): `blender_cast_plugin.zip`
- Files: `io_scene_cast/__init__.py` (directory-resolved; no `PAT_BACKEND_` override)
- Loaded by: Blender, from the backends directory by explicit path (`dev/models.py`); the user's Blender preferences are never touched.

## Manual GUIs the toolkit only downloads

These are pinned so `pat dev setup --only <id>` can fetch and verify them, but no route runs
them: their use is manual, through the upstream GUI, on Windows.

| Program | Upstream | License | Pinned download | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Greyhound 1.46.3.2 | <https://github.com/Scobalula/Greyhound> | GPL-3.0 | windows: `Greyhound.V.1.46.3.2-release.zip` | Original GUI. No agent-controlled live extraction is claimed by this toolkit. |
| Husky 0.8.0.0 | <https://github.com/Scobalula/Husky> | GPL-3.0 | windows: `Husky.0.8.0.0.zip` | Original GUI. Windows live capture through this toolkit is not implemented. |
| C2Mv3 3.0.5 | <https://github.com/o-Astral-o/C2Mv3> | unspecified upstream; binary only | windows: `C2Mv3.zip` | Optional. Upstream publishes a binary without a license; the toolkit downloads it only on explicit request and never redistributes it. Hash pinned from a 2026-09-10 download. |

## Logos

This page uses names and links only. Blender and FFmpeg publish logo policies that allow
referential use; the other projects have not been asked. Logos are a later, per-project
follow-up after asking each maintainer, and none is included yet.
